"4. Brief facts as per the complainant/applicant are that he is into the business of second hand cars sale/purchase business since last 5 years and was approached by the proposed accused persons (a Delhi Police Inspector and a dreaded criminal/gangster) proposing to sell a Mahindra Scorpio car for a total sale consideration of Rs. 11 Lakhs and the proposed accused LOVLEEN persons had demanded Rs. 5 Lakhs in cash as token by LOVLEEN Crl. The complainant paid Rs. 37,000 via bank transfer and Rs. 13,000 in cash to the proposed accused persons the same day and the complainant arranged for the balance token money of Rs. 4.5 Lakhs in cash to be paid the next day. That the moment the complainant handed over Rs. 4.5 Lakhs in cash to the proposed accused persons, the complainant was surrounded by the accomplices / associates of the proposed accused persons claiming to be from Income Tax Department and forcefully made the complainant sit in their car and took him to Sarai Kale Khan and after reaching there the complainant was threatened on gunpoint to dire consequences and false implications in false criminal cases of money laundering and income tax cases. The proposed accused persons had demanded an extortion amount of Rs. 50 Lakhs from the complainant for his and his family's safety. Complainant was forced to leave the city due to fear of the proposed accused persons. Complainant shifted from Hotel Opulence, Udaipur, Rajasthan to Hotel Cygnett Inn Grand, Jaipur Rajasthan along with his wife hiding and staying away from the proposed accused persons. The proposed accused persons after tracking the location of the complainant reached Hotel Cygnett Inn Grand, Jaipur, Rajasthan and abducted & kidnapped the complainant for ransom leaving the complainant's wife at the hotel itself. It is alleged that on the way from Jaipur to Delhi, the complainant was ruthlessly beaten up by the proposed accused persons and was taken to Okhla Police Chowki around 12:30am 1:00am where the complainant was kept captive for 1/2 to 1 hours by the proposed LOVLEEN accused persons and ruthlessly & brutally beaten up by by LOVLEEN Crl. Revision No:387/2024 Sub-Inspector Jai Kumar vs. State page no. 3 of 14 one ASI Jai & Vikas along with the proposed accused persons. Around 2:00 am the complainant was taken to East of Kailash near Sapna Cinema Hall and was held captive for 4 days in the most inhuman condition with his hands and legs tied up without any food and water by the proposed accused persons. The proposed accused persons tortured the complainant for 4 days by ruthlessly & brutally beating him and recording his nude videos and photographs to create pressure upon him and his family to pay the ransom of Rs. 50 Lakhs for the complainant's release. Complainant and his elderly ailing widow mother arranged for the ransom by withdrawing their life savings and LIC insurance money received from the death of the complainant's father and paid it to the proposed accused persons. Complainant was again contacted by the proposed accused persons & threatened to dire consequences with a demand of Rs. 1 Crore and was given a deadline to pay by 20.09.2020. Complainant being aggrieved by the illegal acts of the proposed accused persons running an organised crime syndicate and under fear made a complaint dt. 18.09.2020 to the SHO PS Amar Colony and other Delhi Police higher authorities through speso posts and emails but no action had been taken against the proposed accused persons".

4. That the Revisionist is an Respected Officer of Delhi Police who is presently posted at Inter State Cell, Crime Branch, Chankyapuri, New Delhi. 
5. That the allegations levelled against the Revisionist according to the complaint of the Respondent No. 2 are that "After reaching Delhi, they took me to Okhla Police Chowki where ASI Jai and another police official Vikas where I was Kept for one and a half house and brutally beaten up and made to sign various forms and blank papers.". It is pertinent to mention here that the Revisionist was on active duty at Okhla Industrial Area around of the time of alleged incident. The same fact can be proved through DD entry No. 56A dt. 30.07.2020, Copy of the same is annexed herein as ANNEXURE - C.
6. That the Revisionist and Inspector Rajender @Pahalwan have absolutely no connection with each other and they haven't been in contact with each other during the time frame of the alleged incident,
this absence of proof of nexus between them stands unjustified till date by the Respondent No. 2 which casts a major doubt upon the case of the Respondent No. 2.
7. That Inspector Rajender Singh @Pahalwan was not posted in Okhla Police Chowki and nowhere near Okhla Police Chowki for that matter on the date of alleged incident so the allegation of bringing the Respondent No. 2 to Okhla Police Chowki where the Revisionist beat him is unexplained and thus holds no water.

"(1) The allegations levelled by the complaint in his complaint against Inspector Rajender Singh, ASI Jai Kumar and ASI Vikas have not been substantiated. 
(2) However, on analysis of CDRs of Inspector Rajinder Singh, ASI Jai Kumar, ASI Vikas and Nadir, it has been found that the said police officers are in regular touch with Nadir, who has a criminal record. It generates a strong suspicion that there may be a quid pro quo between them. 
This kind of act/behaviour cannot be accepted in the Department." Copy of the complaint of Respondent No. 2 along with Vigilance verification report. 
9. That the application U/S 156(3) Cr.P.C. of the Respondent No. 2 was previously dismissed by the Ld. JMFC vide order dt. 03.11.2020. Copy of the order of dismissal. 
10. That after the application U/S 156(3) was dismissed the Respondent No. 2 preferred a Revision Petition before the court of Session and the same was allowed and the application was sent back for considering the matter afresh. Copy of the order of the court of Session dt. 05.02.2024.
11. That the ACP Vigilance has highlighted several contradictions in statements and the contents of the complaint of Respondent No. 2, this depicts that the Respondent No. 2 has concocted a story to malign the reputation of the Revisionist. Furthermore, several facts like no calls were made between the Revisionist and the Respondent No. 2 along with the locations extracted from LOVLEEN Crl.
Revision No:387/2024 Sub-Inspector Jai Kumar vs. State page no. 6 of 14 the CDRs clearly shows that the case of Respondent No. 2 rests on blatant lies. 
12. That according to the Vigilance verification Report, the CDR which was analyzed for the date of first alleged incident dt. 18.05.2020 and 19.05.2020 onwards, clearly indicates that the Revisionist and the Respondent No. 2 have had no connectivity with each other and the locations of the Respondent No. 2 are far from the locations of Revisionist.
13. That it is pertinent to mention here that the Vigilance verification report also enquired an independent witness SI Manoj Bhaskar who supported the statements of the Revisionist as "During enquiry, SI Manoj Bhaskar, D- 4904 (PIS No. 16090195) posted as I/C PP Okhla-Phase 3 has stated that ASI Jai Kumar and ASI Vikas were posted in the PP and do emergency duty. On 30.07.2020,
ASI Vikas left the Chowki after completing his duty and gone to his home. The nedt day he returned and continues his duty. ASI Jai Kumar resides in the Police Post itself. On 30.07.2020,  person nameky Ish Kumar was brough in the police post. He further stated that conduct of both the ASIs is good." 
14. That the court of Ld. JMFC failed to appreciate the fact that the vigilance report gave the Revisionist a "Clean Chit" as no case was made out based upon the allegations levelled by the Sub Inspector Jai Kumar vs State on 4 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/177212609/

Meanwhile, the Respondent No. 2 moved before the Delhi High Court and filed a Writ seeking inter alia Police Protection. 
16. That the Respondent No. 2 lodged the present complaint after long thought and planning and filed the complaint after much delay so that the CCTV footages which would prove the innocence of the Revisionist could not be recovered as it is automatically erased after a lapse of 60days. 
17. That the only reason as to why the Respondent No. 2 has dragged the names of honorary officers of Delhi Police as the Revisionist is because the Revisionist stayed in touch with Nadir during an investigation and Nadir Shah helped the Revisionist to catch an accused namely Sachin of Neeraj Bawania Gang in the year 2018. 
18. That the frivolous and misconceived allegations of the Respondent No. 2 is slandering the image/reputation of the Revisionist before the society, and the Respondent No. 2 is enforcing unnecessary and futile litigation upon the Revisionist to fulfil his oblique motives. 
19. That the above said facts clearly shows that the documents, statements given/relied upon by the Respondent No. 2 in the present case are false and fabricated and have been purposely used as evidence by the Respondent No. 2 to obtain favourable orders by deceiving the Court of Law. That this not only casts serious doubts on all the allegations levelled by the Respondent No. 2 against the Revisionist but also creates LOVLEEN great suspicion upon the documents filed by the Respondent No. 2 including the supporting affidavit by LOVLEEN Crl. Revision No:387/2024 Sub-Inspector Jai Kumar vs. State page no. 8 of 14 which seems to be nothing but merely a move to mislead the Hon'ble Court to obtain favourable orders. 
20. That from a bare perusal of the above said facts, it is amply clear that the Respondent No. 2 has himself mislead the court by stating incorrect facts as the same are being contradicted by the Respondent No. 2 himself in the police complaint dt. 18.09.2020, complaint dt. 23.09.2020 annexed with his complaint U/S 200 Cr.P.C.
21. That the Ld. Court of JMFC failed to comply with the order dt. 05.02.2022 passed by the Revisional Court of session wherein the Revisional Court said in Para 19 "......that registration of an FIR against any person entails serious consequences and the consequences become even graver when the allegations are against any public servant as is the case herein, Respondent No. 3, 4 and 5 being officials of Delhi Police. Therefore, a preliminary enquiry in a case of such nature, assumes a lot of importance as it may assist the concerned Magistrate to arrive at a just decision."

5 22. That the Revisionist is an honoured Officer of Delhi Police, promoted out of 10, has an excellent academic history and is a hard-working field officer who has not only dedicated himself to the security of the state of Delhi. 
23. The Revisionist has done exemplary good works for the state of Delhi such as;
i. Firing incident took place in the area of PS Hazrat Nizamuddin on the intervening night of 15-16/04/2018 solved within 36 hours. 
ii. On 13/10/2011 busted a gang of autolifters and recovered 8 stolen vehicles iii. On 26/11/2011 nabbed two desperate criminals Digitally signed by LOVLEEN LOVLEEN Date:
2024.12.04 14:35:30 Crl. Revision No:387/2024 Sub-Inspector Jai Kumar vs. State page no. 9 of 14 +0530 who brutally murdered a Uttar Pradesh Police Constable. (In this case the Revisionist was granted ab A-saadharan Karya Puruskaar by the then Commissioner of Police, Delhi). 
iv. On 19/10/2016 Smashed a Thak-Thak Gang v. Busted a mortuary of dismantled vehicles in Hodal, Haryana. 
24. That no new facts will emerge if the impugned order is allowed to run its course for compliance and no fruitful purpose would be served to initiate investigation against respectable police officers of Delhi Police as the departmental enquiry has already been conducted and no offence was found to have taken place against the Respondent No. 2.
25. That in light of the abovementioned facts and circumstances it is evidence that the impugned order dt. 03.07.2024 passed by the Ld. Court of JMFC suffers from severe irregularities, is bad in law, passed in complete non- application of judicious mind and deserves to be set aside. 
4. It is prayed that the impugned order may be set aside. 
5. The prayer of revisionist has been opposed tooth and nail by the respondent. It is submitted that the impugned order is perfectly legal and justified in the facts and circumstances of this case. It is further submitted that the Vigilance Inquiry conducted by the police LOVLEEN corroborates the allegations levelled by the respondent and is by LOVLEEN Crl. Revision No:387/2024 Sub-Inspector Jai Kumar vs. State page no. 10 of 14 indicative of the unholy nexus of the revisionist with organized criminal gangs. It is further submitted that the respondent is not seeking arrest of the revisionist, rather he seeks a fair investigation. It is further submitted that the respondent has not concocted any allegations and that respondent may be proceeded against u/s 182 IPC if the allegations levelled against the revisionist are found incorrect. As such, his allegations may not be dismissed lightly.

6 6. This court has considered the rival contentions. Records have also been considered. 
7. The entire law regarding exercise of jurisdiction U/s 156(3) Cr.P.C. by a Magistrate has been elaborated recently by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in Alok Kumar Vs. Harsh Mander 2023 SSC Online Del 4219. At Para 40, the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi has observed as under:
"To summarise, a conspectus of the above-mentioned judicial precedents reveal the following :
(i). Power under Section 156(3) Cr. PC necessitates application of judicial mind. 
(ii) Such power is to be exercised in a judicious manner, and cannot be exercised mechanically or arbitrarily. 
(iii) Magistrates cannot direct registration of FIR on mere asking of complainant." 
LOVLEEN Date: 2024.12.04 Crl. Revision No:387/2024 Sub-Inspector Jai Kumar vs. State page no.
11 of 14 8. It is apparent from the above that a Magistrate has to apply his judicial mind while disposing of a prayer U/s 156(3) Cr.P.C. and that directions for registration of an FIR could not be passed in an arbitrary or mechanical manner. 
9. It would be appropriate to reproduce the operative portion of the impugned order for a better understanding of the matter. The relevant extracts are as under:-
"8. This court has considered the preliminary inquiry as well as the report of the Vigilance Department along with the remaining record and submissions on behalf of the applicant. 
9. On perusal of the entire material, this court finds that the allegations made in the application prima facie reveal commission of cognizable offences of such nature that police investigation is imperative. The allegations include kidnapping for ransom at gunpoint, extortion, beating, criminal intimidation which are cognizable offences. 
The Vigilance inquiry led to directions for creating historysheet for proposed accused no. 1 and transfer of proposed accused no.2, 3 and 4 to non- sensitive postings. 
Though there was a delay in filing complaint with the police, the nature of allegations is grave and requires detailed investigation. It is also noteworthy that the area of Sapna Cinema falls within the jurisdiction of PS Amar Colony and this court and the applicant was brought to an office near Sapna Cinema after being abducted from Jaipur, therefore, part of the alleged offence has taken place wihtin the jurisdiction of PS Amar Colony.
Sub Inspector Jai Kumar vs State on 4 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/177212609/
7 LOVLEEN by LOVLEEN Crl. Revision No:387/2024 Sub-Inspector Jai Kumar vs.
State page no. 12 of 14 10. Keeping in mind the totality of the facts and the circumstances, this Court is inclined to invoke the discretionary power vested in the court by virtue of section 156(3) Cr.P.C. as allegations regarding certain cognizable offences have been raised. 
Accordingly the SHO, PS Amar Colony is directed to register an FIR in this case under appropriate sections and submit a compliance report in this regard. It is further directed that the investigation shall not be restricted to the offences alleged in the complaint. It is further made clear that the power to arrest is different from the need to arrest the accused persons. 
11. Keeping in view that some allegations have been levelled against police officials as well, this Court finds it appropriate to direct the DCP (South East) to supervise/
monitor the investigation of the present case"
10. It is observed by this Court that the relevant factual matrix was duly recorded and considered by the Ld. Magistrate in the impugned order. ATR filed by the police as well as the report of Vigilance Department were also considered by the Ld. Magistrate. Having gone through the TCR, this Court must observe that the allegations levelled by the respondent are very grave and serious in nature. 
The kind of evidence required to be collected in this case seems to be beyond the capability of any public person. Recoveries might also need to be effected promptly. The objections raised by the revisionist in the present proceedings are not sufficient to hold that the allegations levelled by the respondent are completely false and fabricated. Infact, Digitally a formal investigation would rather substantiate as to whether or not signed by LOVLEEN LOVLEEN Date:
2024.12.04 14:35:42 Crl. Revision No:387/2024 Sub-Inspector Jai Kumar vs. State page no. 13 of 14 +0530 the infirmities pointed out by the revisionist bear any merits. 
In the entire facts and circumstances, this court does not find any reason to differ from the opinion of Ld. Magistrate. The order passed by Ld. Magistrate does not seem to be arbitrary, perverse or irrational nor does it reflect any jurisdictional error which occasioned any injustice in the matter. The present petition is devoid of any merits and is hereby dismissed. TCR be sent back alongwith a copy of this judgement. 
11. This revision file be consigned to Record Room, as per rules.
